q: A distinctive feature of the working of the Public Accounts Committee is that:

options.A: Its reports are generally unanimous and no minutes of dissent are appended to them
options.B: Its reports are adopted by a majority vote of the members present
options.C: The Chairman of the Committee has a casting vote on all questions
options.D: Any member may record a minute of dissent in the report itself

e: A distinctive feature of the Public Accounts Committee is that it works in a non-partisan manner and its reports are generally unanimous, with no minutes of dissent appended to them.

q: An Audit Para included in the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is treated as finally settled when:

options.A: The Ministry concerned furnishes its Action Taken Note
options.B: One year has elapsed from the laying of the Report before Parliament
options.C: The audit office drops the objection on its own
options.D: The Public Accounts Committee accepts the action taken by the Government on the para

e: An Audit Para is treated as finally settled only when the Public Accounts Committee accepts the action taken by the Government on it; merely furnishing an Action Taken Note does not settle the para.

q: In audit, the concept of 'materiality' refers to:

options.A: The total value of the stores held by the audited unit
options.B: The physical verification of the assets of the audited unit
options.C: The significance of an omission or misstatement of information, judged by whether it could influence the decisions of the users of the accounts
options.D: The minimum amount involved for which a separate audit paragraph is raised

e: Materiality refers to the significance of an omission or misstatement of information, judged by whether it could influence the decisions of the users of the accounts; material matters therefore receive particular audit attention.

q: Indian Government Accounting Standard (IGAS) 2, formulated by the Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board (GASAB), deals with:

options.B: Loans and Advances made by Governments
options.D: Disclosure of prior period items

e: Indian Government Accounting Standard 2, formulated by the Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board, deals with the Accounting and Classification of Grants-in-Aid.

q: The accounts of the Defence Services of the Union are compiled by:

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Defence Accounts Department, headed by the Controller General of Defence Accounts

e: The accounts of the Defence Services of the Union are compiled by the Defence Accounts Department, headed by the Controller General of Defence Accounts.

q: The detailed instructions and procedures governing the audit of the accounts of Indian Railways by the organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India are contained in:

options.B: The Railway Audit Manual issued by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Indian Railway Finance Code

e: The detailed instructions and procedures governing the audit of railway accounts by the Comptroller and Auditor General's organisation are contained in the Railway Audit Manual issued by him.

q: In order to watch the clearance of the objections raised by Audit in the Inspection Reports, the audited office maintains:

options.D: An Objection Book (Register), in which the objections and their settlement are recorded

e: To watch the clearance of objections raised in the Inspection Reports, the audited office maintains an Objection Book or Register in which the objections and their settlement are recorded.

q: Expenditure under a sub-head of a grant exceeds the provision under that sub-head, but the excess is offset by savings under other sub-heads and the total amount of the grant is not exceeded. In such a case:

options.A: An Excess Grant must be voted by Parliament to regularise the excess
options.B: No Excess Grant is required, as regularisation by Parliament is necessary only where the total amount of the grant or appropriation is exceeded
options.C: The FA&CAO can regularise the excess without reporting it anywhere
options.D: The excess under the sub-head is treated as unsanctioned expenditure

e: Regularisation by Parliament through an Excess Grant is required only where the total amount of the grant or appropriation is exceeded; an excess under a sub-head offset by savings elsewhere within the grant needs no Excess Grant.

q: Re-appropriation of funds within a grant is NOT permissible:

options.A: From one sub-head to another sub-head of the same grant
options.B: To meet an anticipated excess under another head of the same grant, where savings are available
options.C: To meet expenditure on a 'new service' or 'new instrument of service' not contemplated in the Budget, without the prior approval of Parliament
options.D: Before the close of the financial year to which it relates

e: Re-appropriation can only redistribute provision already granted; it is not permissible to meet expenditure on a new service or new instrument of service not contemplated in the Budget without the prior approval of Parliament.

q: Interest paid on capital borrowed for the execution of a work, during the period of construction of that work, is ordinarily:

options.A: Charged to the revenue (working expenses) of the year in which it is paid
options.C: Adjusted against the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: Capitalised, that is, charged to the Capital head of the work

e: Interest paid on capital borrowed for the execution of a work during its construction is ordinarily capitalised, that is, charged to the Capital head of the work, as part of its cost.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the classification of Government accounts, a Major Head represents a major function of the Government.
2. A Minor Head under a Major Head represents a programme undertaken to achieve the objectives of that function.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: in the classification of Government accounts, a Major Head represents a major function of the Government, and a Minor Head under it represents a programme undertaken to achieve the objectives of that function.

q: The cash balance held by the Government of India is accounted for as part of:

options.D: None of the three parts of the Government accounts

e: The cash balance held by the Government of India is accounted for as part of the Public Account of India, along with the deposit, remittance and reserve fund balances.

q: Under Article 283 of the Constitution, the custody of the Consolidated Fund of India and the Contingency Fund of India, the payment of moneys into and the withdrawal of moneys from them, and the custody of public moneys other than those credited to the Consolidated Fund, are regulated by:

options.A: Rules made by the Ministry of Finance
options.B: Resolutions of the Public Accounts Committee
options.C: Law made by Parliament or, until such law is made, rules made by the President
options.D: Directions issued by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Under Article 283, the custody of the Consolidated Fund and the Contingency Fund, and the payment of moneys into and withdrawal from them, are regulated by law made by Parliament or, until such law is made, by rules made by the President.

q: Under Article 284 of the Constitution, all moneys received by, or deposited in the custody of, an officer of the Union or a court in connection with the affairs of the Union, other than revenues or public moneys credited to the Consolidated Fund, shall be:

options.A: Paid into the Public Account of India
options.B: Retained by the officer or court receiving them
options.C: Paid into the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Credited to the revenues of the Government

e: Under Article 284, all moneys received by or deposited in the custody of an officer of the Union or a court, other than revenues or public moneys credited to the Consolidated Fund, shall be paid into the Public Account of India.

q: Which of the following does NOT form part of the Appropriation Accounts of a grant?

options.A: The grant-wise summary showing the final grant, the actual expenditure and the excess or saving
options.B: Explanations for the variations between the actual expenditure and the final grant
options.C: The certificate of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Profit and Loss Account of the Railway undertaking

e: The Appropriation Accounts contain the grant-wise summary of final grant, actual expenditure and excess or saving, explanations for the variations and the certificate of the Comptroller and Auditor General; a Profit and Loss Account of the undertaking forms no part of them.

q: Large and persistent savings under a grant, noticed year after year, are regarded in audit as indicative of:

options.A: Efficient financial management by the executive
options.B: Defective budgeting, that is, framing of estimates on the higher side without a proper assessment of the requirements
options.D: Prompt surrender of funds by the spending authorities

e: Large and persistent savings under a grant, noticed year after year, indicate defective budgeting, that is, estimates framed on the higher side without a proper assessment of the requirements.

q: The 'escape clause' in the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) framework permits the Government to deviate from the fiscal deficit target, in exceptional circumstances such as national security, war or national calamity, up to:

options.D: 0.25 per cent of GDP

e: The escape clause in the FRBM framework permits the Government to deviate from the fiscal deficit target in exceptional circumstances such as national security, war or national calamity, but only up to 0.5 per cent of GDP.

q: The FRBM Review Committee, which reviewed the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act in 2016 and recommended a debt-based fiscal framework, was chaired by:

options.D: Shaktikanta Das

e: The FRBM Review Committee, which reviewed the Act in 2016 and recommended a debt-based fiscal framework, was chaired by Shri N. K. Singh, and the Act was amended on its recommendations.

q: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management framework, as amended following the recommendations of the FRBM Review Committee, prescribes for the Central Government a debt ceiling of:

options.D: 40 per cent of GDP

e: The FRBM framework, as amended following the recommendations of the FRBM Review Committee, prescribes for the Central Government a debt ceiling of 40 per cent of GDP.

q: The assurance which a financial (attest) audit provides that the financial statements are free from material misstatement is:

options.A: Absolute assurance that no error or fraud exists
options.C: Reasonable assurance, which is a high level of assurance but not a guarantee
options.D: Assurance confined to the arithmetical accuracy of the accounts

e: A financial audit provides reasonable assurance, which is a high level of assurance that the financial statements are free from material misstatement, but it is not an absolute guarantee that no error or fraud exists.

q: The primary responsibility for the prevention and detection of fraud and error in an organisation rests with:

options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The management of the organisation

e: The primary responsibility for the prevention and detection of fraud and error in an organisation rests with its management; the auditor plans and performs the audit to obtain reasonable assurance, but does not own that responsibility.

q: An Inspection Report issued by the audit office after local audit of a unit is ordinarily divided into:

options.A: Part I, containing serious irregularities requiring the attention of higher authorities, and Part II, containing other, less serious irregularities
options.B: Part I, containing the accounts of the unit, and Part II, containing the audit findings
options.C: Part I, meant for the Railway Board, and Part II, meant for the zonal Railway
options.D: It is not divided into parts at all

e: An Inspection Report is ordinarily divided into Part I, containing serious irregularities requiring the attention of higher authorities, and Part II, containing other, less serious irregularities.

q: Where a loss of public money or stores occurs by reason of fraud, negligence or any other cause, the financial rules require that the loss should be reported promptly to:

options.B: The Accounts and Audit authorities and the next higher administrative authority
options.D: The Finance Commission

e: Where a loss of public money or stores occurs by reason of fraud, negligence or any other cause, the financial rules require the loss to be reported promptly to the Accounts and Audit authorities and the next higher administrative authority.

q: Under Article 292 of the Constitution, the executive power of the Union extends to borrowing upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of India:

options.B: Only from the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: Within such limits, if any, as may be fixed by Parliament by law
options.D: Only for financing railway projects

e: Under Article 292, the executive power of the Union extends to borrowing upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of India within such limits, if any, as may be fixed by Parliament by law.

q: A zonal railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 5,000 crore, ordinary working expenses of Rs 3,700 crore, appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund of Rs 300 crore and appropriation to the Pension Fund of Rs 200 crore. Its Operating Ratio is:
e: Gross working expenses = 3,700 + 300 + 200 = Rs 4,200 crore; Operating Ratio = 4,200 / 5,000 x 100 = 84 per cent.

q: A railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 8,400 crore and working expenses, including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, of Rs 7,150 crore. Its net revenue is:

options.D: Rs 1,250 crore

e: Net revenue = gross traffic earnings - working expenses = 8,400 - 7,150 = Rs 1,250 crore.

q: The net revenue of a railway is Rs 900 crore and its capital-at-charge is Rs 12,000 crore. The return on capital-at-charge of the railway is:
e: Return on capital-at-charge = net revenue / capital-at-charge x 100 = 900 / 12,000 x 100 = 7.5 per cent.

q: Under the pre-merger financial convention, the dividend payable by a railway on a capital-at-charge (excluding the capital invested in strategic lines) of Rs 18,000 crore, at the rate of 4 per cent per annum, would amount to:

options.D: Rs 720 crore

e: Dividend = 4 per cent of the capital-at-charge of Rs 18,000 crore = Rs 720 crore, the capital invested in strategic lines being excluded from the dividend-bearing capital.

q: A railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 7,500 crore, working expenses (including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund) of Rs 6,900 crore and dividend payable to General Finances of Rs 250 crore. Its surplus is:

options.D: Rs 350 crore

e: Net revenue = 7,500 - 6,900 = Rs 600 crore; surplus = net revenue - dividend payable = 600 - 250 = Rs 350 crore.

q: The reports of the Estimates Committee are presented to:

options.D: The Public Accounts Committee

e: The reports of the Estimates Committee are presented to the Lok Sabha only, as the Committee is a committee of that House.

q: Which of the following is a recognised feature of a sound system of internal control?

options.A: Rotation of duties among the staff from time to time, so that the same official does not continue indefinitely on the same work
options.B: Allowing one official to handle both the cash and the accounts of a transaction
options.C: Dispensing with independent verification of the work done
options.D: Checking of all transactions only at the end of the financial year

e: Rotation of duties among the staff from time to time is a sound internal control: it prevents the same official from handling the same work indefinitely, deters irregularities and gets the work seen by another hand.

q: At the sittings of the Public Accounts Committee, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, or his representative:

options.A: Presides over the sittings of the Committee
options.B: Attends to assist the Committee with his expert advice on the audit paragraphs under examination
options.C: Presents the case of the Government on the audit paragraphs
options.D: Records the minutes of the Committee

e: At the sittings of the Public Accounts Committee, the Comptroller and Auditor General, or his representative, attends to assist the Committee with his expert advice on the audit paragraphs under examination.

q: Unlike the grants voted by Parliament, which lapse at the close of the financial year, the balances of the railway reserve funds, such as the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, held in the Public Account of India:

options.A: Also lapse at the close of the financial year
options.B: Are transferred to the Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Do not lapse and are carried forward for utilisation in the following years
options.D: Are refunded to General Finances at the close of the year

e: Unlike the grants voted by Parliament, which lapse at the close of the financial year, the balances of the railway reserve funds held in the Public Account do not lapse and are carried forward for utilisation in the following years.

q: The examination of the estimates by the Estimates Committee is:

options.A: Carried out only during the Budget session of Parliament
options.B: Carried out only once in five years
options.C: A continuous process, the Committee examining selected subjects and Ministries throughout the year and reporting to the Lok Sabha as it proceeds
options.D: Carried out after the accounts of the year have been closed

e: The examination of estimates by the Estimates Committee is a continuous process: the Committee examines selected subjects and Ministries throughout the year and reports to the Lok Sabha as it proceeds.

q: Under Article 280(3) of the Constitution, it is also the duty of the Finance Commission to make recommendations to the President as to:

options.A: The principles which should govern the grants-in-aid of the revenues of the States out of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: The principles governing the classification of Government accounts
options.C: The rate of dividend payable by Railways to General Finances
options.D: The salaries and allowances of the Judges of the Supreme Court

e: Under Article 280(3), it is also the duty of the Finance Commission to make recommendations to the President as to the principles which should govern the grants-in-aid of the revenues of the States out of the Consolidated Fund of India.

q: The corpus of the Contingency Fund of India was enhanced by the Finance Act, 2020 from Rs 500 crore to:

options.D: Rs 50,000 crore

e: The corpus of the Contingency Fund of India was enhanced by the Finance Act, 2020 from Rs 500 crore to Rs 30,000 crore, so as to give the Government a larger cushion for unforeseen expenditure.

q: The Contingency Fund of India is in the nature of:

options.A: An imprest placed at the disposal of the President to enable advances to be made for meeting unforeseen expenditure, pending authorisation by Parliament
options.B: A deposit account forming part of the Public Account of India
options.C: A reserve fund built up out of the surplus revenues of the Government
options.D: A fund fed by market borrowings raised by the Government

e: The Contingency Fund is in the nature of an imprest placed at the disposal of the President to enable advances to be made for meeting unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament, the advances being recouped thereafter.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 268 of the Constitution, certain duties, such as stamp duties, are levied by the Union but are collected and appropriated by the States.
2. Under Article 270 of the Constitution, all taxes and duties in the Union List, other than those referred to in Articles 268 and 269 and any surcharge or cess, are shared between the Union and the States.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: under Article 268, duties such as stamp duties are levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States; under Article 270, all other Union List taxes and duties, except surcharge and cess, are shared with the States.

q: Under Article 293 of the Constitution, the executive power of a State extends to borrowing:

options.A: Only from the Reserve Bank of India
options.B: From foreign governments and international institutions directly
options.D: Within the territory of India upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of the State, within such limits as may be fixed by the Legislature of the State by law

e: Under Article 293, the executive power of a State extends to borrowing within the territory of India upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of the State, within such limits as may be fixed by the Legislature of the State by law.

q: Article 274 of the Constitution requires that a Bill which imposes or varies any tax or duty in which the States are interested shall not be introduced in either House of Parliament except:

options.A: On the recommendation of the President
options.B: With the concurrence of the Inter-State Council
options.C: With the approval of the Finance Commission
options.D: After consultation with all the State Governments

e: Article 274 requires that a Bill which imposes or varies any tax or duty in which the States are interested shall not be introduced in either House of Parliament except on the recommendation of the President.

q: The levy and collection of Goods and Services Tax on supplies in the course of inter-State trade or commerce, and its apportionment between the Union and the States, are provided for in the Constitution under:

options.D: Article 271

e: The levy and collection of Goods and Services Tax on supplies in the course of inter-State trade or commerce, and its apportionment between the Union and the States, are provided for under Article 269A.

q: The qualifications of the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission, and the manner in which they are to be selected, are determined by:

options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Parliament, by law

e: The qualifications of the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission, and the manner in which they are to be selected, are determined by Parliament by law, and not left to executive discretion.

q: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended that the share of the States in the net proceeds of the divisible pool of central taxes (vertical devolution) should be:

options.D: 45 per cent

e: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended that the share of the States in the net proceeds of the divisible pool of central taxes, that is, the vertical devolution, should be 41 per cent.

q: For the purpose of distribution of taxes between the Union and the States, the expression 'net proceeds' of a tax or duty means:

options.A: The proceeds of the tax or duty reduced by the cost of collection
options.B: The gross collections of the tax or duty
options.C: The proceeds of the tax or duty after deducting refunds only
options.D: The proceeds of the tax or duty divided equally between the Union and the States

e: For distribution between the Union and the States, the net proceeds of a tax or duty means the proceeds of that tax or duty reduced by the cost of collection.

q: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 came into force in the year:
e: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 was brought into force in the year 2004, the year following its enactment.

q: Under the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management framework, the Central Government shall not give guarantees aggregating to an amount exceeding the following, in any financial year:

options.D: 5 per cent of GDP

e: Under the FRBM framework, the Central Government shall not give guarantees aggregating to an amount exceeding 0.5 per cent of GDP in any financial year.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 lays down the fiscal responsibility targets for the Central Government.
2. The States have enacted their own Fiscal Responsibility Legislations prescribing deficit and debt targets for themselves.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the FRBM Act, 2003 lays down the fiscal responsibility targets for the Central Government, and the States have enacted their own Fiscal Responsibility Legislations prescribing deficit and debt targets for themselves.

q: Under the fiscal responsibility framework applicable to the States, the fiscal deficit of a State is targeted to be contained within:

options.A: 5 per cent of its Gross State Domestic Product
options.C: 1 per cent of its Gross State Domestic Product
options.D: 3 per cent of its Gross State Domestic Product

e: Under the fiscal responsibility framework applicable to the States, the fiscal deficit of a State is targeted to be contained within 3 per cent of its Gross State Domestic Product.

q: The FRBM Review Committee of 2016 recommended an overall debt ceiling for the general Government (the Centre and the States together) of:

options.A: 60 per cent of GDP - 40 per cent for the Centre and 20 per cent for the States
options.D: 40 per cent of GDP for the Centre and the States together

e: The FRBM Review Committee of 2016 recommended an overall debt ceiling for the general Government of 60 per cent of GDP, comprising 40 per cent for the Centre and 20 per cent for the States.

q: The classification of Government expenditure into 'Plan' and 'Non-Plan' was discontinued in the Union Budget with effect from the Budget for:
e: The classification of Government expenditure into Plan and Non-Plan was discontinued in the Union Budget with effect from the Budget for 2017-18.

q: Since the Budget for 2017-18, the Union Budget is presented to Parliament on:

options.A: The last working day of February
options.D: 1 February

e: Advancing the Budget presentation to 1 February from 2017-18 ensures that the Appropriation Act and Finance Act are passed before the financial year begins on 1 April, so that spending can start from the first day of the year.

q: The proceeds realised by the Government from disinvestment of its shareholding in public sector undertakings are classified in the Union Budget as:

options.D: Public debt

e: Disinvestment receipts do not create any liability or future repayment obligation for the Government; they are therefore treated as non-debt capital receipts, unlike borrowings which add to debt.

q: In the accounts and Budget documents of the Government of India, the collections under the small savings schemes and the balances of Provident Funds are shown as:

options.A: 'Other liabilities' of the Government, distinct from its public debt
options.B: A part of the public debt of India
options.C: Revenue receipts of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: Charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India

e: Small savings collections and provident fund balances are liabilities administered through the Public Account; in fiscal presentation they are grouped as 'other liabilities' of the Government, kept distinct from the public debt proper.

q: The total expenditure of the Government of India for a year is Rs 45,00,000 crore, its revenue receipts are Rs 32,00,000 crore and its non-debt capital receipts (recoveries of loans and disinvestment proceeds) are Rs 1,00,000 crore. The fiscal deficit of the Government for the year is:

options.D: Rs 12,00,000 crore

e: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure - (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts) = 45,00,000 - (32,00,000 + 1,00,000) = Rs 12,00,000 crore.

q: The fiscal deficit of the Government for a year is Rs 9,60,000 crore and the interest payments during the year are Rs 6,40,000 crore. The primary deficit of the Government for the year is:

options.D: Rs 6,40,000 crore

e: Primary deficit = fiscal deficit - interest payments = 9,60,000 - 6,40,000 = Rs 3,20,000 crore; it measures the borrowing need apart from interest on past debt.

q: Complete Parliamentary control over the public finances of the Union implies that the executive cannot:

options.A: Operate the Public Account of India
options.B: Levy any tax, raise any loan or incur any expenditure without the authority of Parliament
options.C: Maintain commercial accounts for departmental undertakings
options.D: Present the Budget without the approval of the Estimates Committee

e: Complete parliamentary control over public finance means the executive cannot levy any tax, raise any loan or incur any expenditure without the authority of Parliament.

q: Indian Government Accounting Standard (IGAS) 1, formulated by the Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board, deals with:

options.B: Loans and advances made by Governments
options.C: Accounting for fixed assets of Governments
options.D: Guarantees given by Governments - disclosure requirements

e: IGAS 1, issued by the Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board, prescribes the disclosure requirements to be followed by Governments in respect of guarantees given by them.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian Government Accounting Standards (IGAS) issued so far are based on the cash basis of accounting followed in Government accounts.
2. The Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board is engaged in formulating accrual-based Indian Government Financial Reporting Standards (IGFRS).
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the IGAS issued so far are framed on the cash basis followed in Government accounts, and GASAB is simultaneously formulating accrual-based IGFRS for the shift towards accrual reporting.

q: While examining the accounts of the Government, the Public Accounts Committee is also required to satisfy itself that:

options.A: The estimates framed for the following year are realistic
options.B: Every re-appropriation of funds has been made in accordance with the provisions of the rules made in that behalf
options.C: The rate of dividend payable by Railways to General Finances is adequate
options.D: The public undertakings are managed on sound business principles

e: Among its duties, the Public Accounts Committee must satisfy itself that every re-appropriation of funds has been made in accordance with the provisions of the rules made in that behalf.

q: In the Indian system of audit, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India:

options.A: Can disallow any item of expenditure and surcharge the officer responsible for it
options.B: Can stop payment of any bill which he considers irregular
options.C: Exercises pre-audit over all expenditure of Indian Railways
options.D: Has no power to disallow expenditure or to stop payment, and brings irregularities to notice through his Reports submitted to the President

e: The CAG of India has no power to disallow expenditure or to stop payment; he audits after the event and brings irregularities to notice through his Audit Reports submitted to the President.

q: For the audit of Government companies, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is assisted by an 'Audit Board', which consists of:

options.A: Officers of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department together with outside experts in the relevant fields
options.B: Only the statutory auditors of the companies concerned
options.C: Members of the Committee on Public Undertakings
options.D: Representatives of the administrative Ministries only

e: For the audit of Government companies, the CAG is assisted by an Audit Board consisting of officers of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department together with outside experts in the relevant fields.

q: Financial (attest) audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is concerned with determining whether:

options.A: The programmes of the audited entity have achieved their objectives
options.B: The financial statements of the audited entity are prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework
options.C: The transactions of the audited entity conform to the applicable laws and regulations
options.D: The staff strength of the audited entity is adequate for its work

e: Financial or attest audit is concerned with determining whether the financial statements of the audited entity are prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The scope and extent of statutory audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India are governed by the Constitution and the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971.
2. The scope, coverage and frequency of internal audit are determined by the management of the organisation itself.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the scope of the CAG's statutory audit is governed by the Constitution and the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, while the scope, coverage and frequency of internal audit are determined by the management itself.

q: The amounts authorised by the Appropriation Act for withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India are specified, service-wise and purpose-wise, in:

options.A: The Schedule appended to the Appropriation Act
options.D: The Demands for Grants of the Ministries

e: The amounts authorised by the Appropriation Act for withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund of India are specified, service-wise and purpose-wise, in the Schedule appended to the Appropriation Act.

q: After the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget, the expenditure of the Ministry of Railways is presented to Parliament:

options.A: Through sixteen separate Demands for Grants, as before the merger
options.B: Only as charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Through the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Finance
options.D: Through a single Demand for Grant of the Ministry of Railways

e: After the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget, the expenditure of the Ministry of Railways is presented through a single Demand for Grant of that Ministry, instead of sixteen separate Demands.

q: The management of the public debt of the Government of India, including the issue and servicing of market loans and treasury bills, is entrusted to:

options.C: The Securities and Exchange Board of India
options.D: The Indian Banks' Association

e: The Reserve Bank of India is entrusted with the management of the public debt of the Government of India, including the issue and servicing of market loans and treasury bills.

q: Treasury Bills of the Government of India are issued for maturities of:

options.D: 1 year, 2 years and 5 years

e: Treasury Bills of the Government of India are issued in three standard maturities of 91 days, 182 days and 364 days, to meet short-term cash requirements.

q: The special securities issued by the Government of India to the National Small Savings Fund against the net collections under the small savings schemes form part of:

options.D: The charged expenditure of the year

e: The special securities issued to the National Small Savings Fund against net small savings collections are Government securities held internally, and hence form part of the internal debt of India.

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India comprehensively revised the Regulations on Audit and Accounts, superseding the earlier Regulations of 2007, in the year:
e: The CAG comprehensively revised the Regulations on Audit and Accounts in the year 2020, superseding the earlier Regulations of 2007.

q: The Public Financial Management System (PFMS), the platform used for payment, accounting and monitoring of the flow of funds under Government schemes, is managed by:

options.B: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Controller General of Accounts, Ministry of Finance

e: The Public Financial Management System, used for payment, accounting and monitoring of funds under Government schemes, is managed by the Controller General of Accounts in the Ministry of Finance.

q: Under the cash basis of accounting followed in Government accounts, stores are received in a Government office in March 2026, but the supplier's bill is paid in April 2026. The expenditure will be accounted for in the accounts of:

options.A: 2025-26, the year in which the stores were received
options.C: 2026-27, the year in which the payment is actually made
options.D: The year in which the supplier's bill is received in the office

e: Under the cash basis of accounting, expenditure is booked in the year in which payment is actually made, not when the stores are received; hence this payment falls in the accounts of 2026-27.

q: A zonal railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 5,000 crore, ordinary working expenses of Rs 3,900 crore, appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund of Rs 250 crore and appropriation to the Pension Fund of Rs 250 crore. Its Operating Ratio is:

options.D: 90 per cent

e: Operating Ratio = total working expenses x 100 / gross traffic earnings = (3,900 + 250 + 250) x 100 / 5,000 = 88 per cent, the DRF and Pension Fund appropriations forming part of working expenses.

q: A railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 9,600 crore and working expenses, including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, of Rs 8,150 crore. Its net revenue is:

options.D: Rs 1,450 crore

e: Net revenue = gross traffic earnings - working expenses = 9,600 - 8,150 = Rs 1,450 crore.

q: The net revenue of a railway is Rs 880 crore and its capital-at-charge is Rs 11,000 crore. The return on capital-at-charge of the railway is:

options.D: 12.5 per cent

e: Return on capital-at-charge = net revenue x 100 / capital-at-charge = 880 x 100 / 11,000 = 8 per cent.

q: Under the pre-merger financial convention, the dividend payable by a railway on a capital-at-charge (excluding the capital invested in strategic lines) of Rs 22,500 crore, at the rate of 4 per cent per annum, would amount to:

options.D: Rs 2,250 crore

e: Dividend = 4 per cent of the dividend-bearing capital-at-charge = 4 x 22,500 / 100 = Rs 900 crore, capital invested in strategic lines being excluded.

q: A railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 6,300 crore, working expenses (including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund) of Rs 5,600 crore and dividend payable to General Finances of Rs 400 crore. Its surplus is:

options.D: Rs 100 crore

e: Surplus = net revenue - dividend payable = (6,300 - 5,600) - 400 = 700 - 400 = Rs 300 crore.

q: If expenditure of a revenue nature is incorrectly charged to Capital in the railway accounts, the immediate effect is that:

options.A: The working expenses and the Operating Ratio are overstated
options.B: The working expenses and the Operating Ratio are understated, while the net revenue and the capital-at-charge are overstated
options.C: The gross traffic earnings are overstated
options.D: There is no effect on the financial results of the Railway

e: Charging revenue expenditure to Capital keeps it out of working expenses, so working expenses and the Operating Ratio are understated, while net revenue and capital-at-charge are overstated.

q: The Profit and Loss Account and the Balance Sheet of Indian Railways, prepared to ascertain the commercial results of the undertaking, are in the nature of:

options.A: Statutory accounts of a company under the Companies Act, 2013
options.B: Accounts maintained by the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: Proforma accounts prepared within the framework of the Government accounts
options.D: Annexures appended to the Finance Bill

e: The Profit and Loss Account and Balance Sheet of the Railways are proforma accounts, prepared within the framework of the Government accounts to bring out the commercial results of the undertaking.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 246A of the Constitution confers simultaneous power on Parliament and on the Legislature of every State to make laws with respect to Goods and Services Tax.
2. Parliament alone has the exclusive power to make laws with respect to Goods and Services Tax on supplies in the course of inter-State trade or commerce.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: Article 246A confers simultaneous power on Parliament and State Legislatures to make GST laws, but Parliament alone has the exclusive power for GST on supplies in the course of inter-State trade or commerce.

q: A Proclamation of Financial Emergency under Article 360 of the Constitution:

options.C: Was issued during the COVID-19 pandemic
options.D: Has never been issued in India so far

e: A Proclamation of Financial Emergency under Article 360 has never been issued in India so far, not even during the 1991 balance of payments crisis or the COVID-19 pandemic.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 285 of the Constitution, the property of the Union is exempt from all taxes imposed by a State or by any authority within a State, unless Parliament otherwise provides by law.
2. Under Article 289 of the Constitution, the property and income of a State are exempt from Union taxation, though this exemption does not extend to a trade or business carried on by or on behalf of the Government of a State.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: Article 285 exempts Union property from State taxation unless Parliament provides otherwise, and Article 289 exempts State property and income from Union taxation, except a trade or business carried on by or on behalf of the State Government.

q: Under Article 293(3) of the Constitution, a State may not, without the consent of the Government of India, raise any loan if:

options.A: The State has a revenue deficit in the previous financial year
options.B: Any part of a loan granted to it by the Government of India (or its predecessor Government) remains outstanding, or a loan in respect of which the Government of India has given a guarantee remains outstanding
options.C: The loan is proposed to be raised from the open market
options.D: The State Legislature has not fixed the borrowing limit by law

e: Under Article 293(3), a State may not raise any loan without the consent of the Government of India if any part of a loan granted by the Centre, or of a loan guaranteed by it, remains outstanding.

q: Property accruing to the Government by escheat or lapse, or as bona vacantia, in respect of property situated within a State, vests under Article 296 of the Constitution in:

options.C: The Collector of the district, to be held in trust for the public
options.D: The person who last possessed the property

e: Under Article 296, property accruing by escheat or lapse, or as bona vacantia, in respect of property situated within a State vests in the Government of that State.

q: Under Article 243-I of the Constitution, the State Finance Commission, which reviews the financial position of the Panchayats and the Municipalities, is constituted by:

options.A: The President of India, every ten years
options.B: The Union Finance Minister, along with the Union Finance Commission
options.C: The State Legislature, by a resolution passed each year
options.D: The Governor of the State, at the expiration of every fifth year

e: Under Article 243-I, the State Finance Commission is constituted by the Governor of the State at the expiration of every fifth year to review the financial position of the Panchayats and Municipalities.

q: Under Article 280(3) of the Constitution, the Finance Commission of India is also required to make recommendations as to the measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of the Panchayats and Municipalities in the State, on the basis of the recommendations made by:

options.A: The National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog)
options.B: The Finance Commission of the State
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Under Article 280(3), the Finance Commission recommends measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities, on the basis of the recommendations made by the State Finance Commission.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Goods and Services Tax Council:
1. In the voting in the Council, the vote of the Central Government carries a weightage of one-third of the total votes cast.
2. The votes of all the State Governments taken together carry a weightage of two-thirds of the total votes cast, and every decision requires a majority of not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of the members present and voting.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: in the GST Council, the Centre's vote carries a weightage of one-third and the States' votes together two-thirds of the votes cast, and every decision needs a majority of not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes.

q: The Goods and Services Tax Compensation Fund, into which the proceeds of the compensation cess are credited and from which compensation is paid to the States for loss of revenue on account of the introduction of GST, forms part of:

options.C: The Consolidated Fund of the States collectively
options.D: The Public Account of India

e: The GST Compensation Fund is kept in the Public Account of India, the compensation cess credited to it being held for the specific purpose of compensating the States.

q: In the horizontal devolution of the divisible pool of central taxes among the States recommended by the Fifteenth Finance Commission, the criterion carrying the largest weight (45 per cent) is:

options.D: Demographic performance

e: In the Fifteenth Finance Commission's horizontal devolution formula, income distance, which measures how far a State's per capita income is from that of the highest income State, carries the largest weight of 45 per cent.

q: The 'Effective Revenue Deficit' of the Central Government, a concept introduced in the fiscal responsibility framework, is defined as the:

options.A: Revenue deficit minus the interest payments of the Government
options.B: Revenue deficit minus the grants-in-aid given by the Central Government to the States and others for the creation of capital assets
options.C: Fiscal deficit minus the revenue deficit
options.D: Excess of revenue expenditure over total receipts of the Government

e: Effective Revenue Deficit is the revenue deficit minus the grants-in-aid given by the Centre to the States and others for the creation of capital assets, since such grants, though booked as revenue expenditure, create assets.

q: The Medium-term Expenditure Framework statement, which is laid before Parliament along with the Budget under the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management framework, primarily sets out:

options.A: The audited expenditure of the Government for the preceding three years
options.B: The demands for grants of all Ministries for the ensuing year
options.C: A three-year rolling target for the expenditure indicators of the Government, with the underlying assumptions
options.D: The list of new schemes proposed to be taken up during the year

e: The Medium-term Expenditure Framework statement sets out a three-year rolling target for the expenditure indicators of the Government, along with the underlying assumptions, under the FRBM framework.

q: The 'Revenue Deficit' of the Government for a year represents the excess of:

options.A: Total expenditure over total receipts of the Government
options.B: Revenue expenditure over the total receipts of the Government
options.C: Capital expenditure over capital receipts of the Government
options.D: Revenue expenditure over revenue receipts of the Government

e: Revenue deficit represents the excess of the revenue expenditure of the Government over its revenue receipts for the year.

q: Which one of the following is NOT a section of the Public Account of India in the Government system of accounts?

options.D: Deposits and Advances

e: Public Debt is accounted for under the Consolidated Fund of India, not the Public Account; the Public Account covers sections such as Small Savings and Provident Funds, Reserve Funds, and Deposits and Advances.

q: In the Government system of accounts, a recovery of an overpayment made to a Government servant in an earlier year is generally adjusted as:

options.A: A miscellaneous receipt of the Government
options.B: A non-tax revenue receipt of the year of recovery
options.C: A capital receipt of the Government
options.D: A reduction (deduct entry) of the expenditure under the head to which the original payment was charged

e: A recovery of an overpayment made in an earlier year is generally adjusted as a reduction, that is a deduct entry, of the expenditure under the head to which the original payment was charged.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Transactions between Indian Railways and other Government departments, such as Defence and Posts, are settled by actual cash payment through treasuries in every case.
2. Such inter-departmental transactions are ordinarily settled by book adjustment through the Central Accounts Section of the Reserve Bank of India at Nagpur, without any actual cash payment.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false, as such transactions are not settled by cash payment in every case; statement 2 is true, since inter-departmental transactions are ordinarily settled by book adjustment through the Central Accounts Section of the Reserve Bank of India at Nagpur.

q: According to the first canon of financial propriety, every public officer is expected to exercise, in respect of expenditure incurred from public moneys, the same vigilance as:

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India exercises in audit
options.B: A person of ordinary prudence would exercise in respect of expenditure of his own money
options.C: The Finance Ministry prescribes in the Budget estimates
options.D: A commercial undertaking exercises in spending its own capital

e: The first canon of financial propriety expects every public officer to exercise, over expenditure from public moneys, the same vigilance as a person of ordinary prudence would exercise in spending his own money.

q: In the States, the office which compiles the accounts of the State Government and deals with entitlement functions such as provident fund accounts and authorisation of pensionary benefits is the office of the:

options.B: Principal Accountant General (General and Social Sector Audit)
options.D: Director of Treasuries of the State

e: In the States, the Accountant General (Accounts and Entitlement) compiles the accounts of the State Government and deals with entitlement functions such as provident fund accounts and authorisation of pensionary benefits.

q: Under the departmentalised system of accounts of the Union Government introduced in 1976, the payments of the civil Ministries and Departments are made through:

options.A: The district treasuries of the State Governments
options.B: The office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: Pay and Accounts Offices functioning under the respective Ministries, under the overall guidance of the Controller General of Accounts
options.D: The Reserve Bank of India directly to the claimants

e: Under the departmentalised system introduced in 1976, payments of the civil Ministries are made through Pay and Accounts Offices functioning under the respective Ministries, under the overall guidance of the Controller General of Accounts.

q: The district treasuries functioning under a State Government render their monthly accounts, for compilation into the accounts of the State, to the:

options.B: Accountant General (Accounts and Entitlement) of the State
options.C: Finance Department of the State Government
options.D: Controller General of Accounts, Government of India

e: District treasuries render their monthly accounts, for compilation into the accounts of the State, to the Accountant General (Accounts and Entitlement) of the State.

q:
Consider the following statements about the accounting reforms undertaken on Indian Railways:
1. The statutory accounts of Indian Railways continue to form part of the Government accounts and are maintained on the cash basis.
2. As part of the accounting reforms, accrual-based financial statements have been prepared with the technical support of the Accounting Research Foundation of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, so as to ascertain the true cost of services and the financial position of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the statutory accounts of the Railways form part of the Government accounts on the cash basis, and accrual-based financial statements have been prepared under the accounting reforms with the technical support of the Accounting Research Foundation of the ICAI.

q: AIMS, the computerised system being implemented on Indian Railways as part of the accounting reforms for the preparation and maintenance of accounts, stands for:

options.D: Asset Information Management System

e: AIMS stands for Accounting Information Management System, the computerised system implemented on Indian Railways under the accounting reforms for the preparation and maintenance of accounts.
